name: voyager-3d
description: Create 3D models, game assets and renders from chat. Voyager 3D brings AI 3D model generation, a searchable library of 3D assets, textures and HDRIs, and Blender rendering on cloud GPUs together, for game development, product visualization, previs, animation and 3D design.

interface.longDescription:
Create 3D models, game assets and renders from chat. Voyager 3D brings AI 3D model generation, a searchable library of 3D assets, textures and HDRIs, and Blender rendering on cloud GPUs together, for game development, product visualization, previs, animation and 3D design.

Generate 3D models with AI. Turn a text prompt or an image into a textured 3D model. Retexture it, auto-rig it, add animation, and download it as GLB for Unity, Unreal, Godot, Blender or any 3D app. Models come from leading 3D generators including Meshy, Tripo, Rodin and Hunyuan3D.

Find ready-made 3D assets. Search the Voyager library in plain words ("weathered wooden chair", "studio HDRI") for 3D models, PBR materials and textures, HDRI skies and character animations, each at real-world scale with its licence. Or bring your own GLB, FBX, OBJ or USD.

Render on cloud GPUs. Make product renders, turntables, stills and short videos with Blender or Vork, Voyager's fast Blender-compatible renderer, on a cloud GPU machine. No local GPU needed. You see an estimate before anything runs, previews before the final render, and download links when it's done. Machines pause on their own when idle.

Sign in with your Voyager account. No desktop app needed.
defaultPrompt: Use Voyager 3D to find a ready-made armchair model and render a 1080p studio product shot of it.
Use Voyager 3D to generate a 3D model of a ceramic teapot and render it in a studio still with Blender.
Use Voyager 3D to render a 5-second turntable video of this GLB model with Blender.

positive.description: Searching the asset library shows real models with previews, sizes and licences, and leases nothing.
positive.prompt: Find a ready-made 3D model of a wooden chair I could render, and show me the best options.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls assets_search with a short query (kind model). Shows the best few hits with their preview images, names and real-world sizes in metres, and may call assets_show on one for its files, licence (CC0) and credit. Leases no machine and spends no credits; offers to render one if the reviewer wants.

positive.description: An estimate is given before anything is leased, and nothing is leased without approval.
positive.prompt: How long would a 10-second 1080p Vork render take on a cloud GPU, and roughly what would it cost? Don't start anything yet.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls estimate_render for about 240 frames (10 s at 24 fps) at 1080p with the std/final profile on the default render preset, then states the GPU and the rough time and cost range it returns, may mention a faster multi-GPU alternative it lists, and says the numbers are rough until a preview of the actual scene is timed. Calls no create_machine and leases nothing.

positive.description: A full Blender still render on one machine, from lease to release, with a library model.
positive.prompt: Render a 1080p studio still of a ready-made armchair from the Voyager library with Blender. You have my OK to lease one render-lite machine; release it when done.
positive.tools_triggered: assets_search, list_presets, create_machine, get_machine, run_command, upload_files, download_files, release_machine
positive.expected_behavior: Finds an armchair with assets_search, states the render-lite GPU and its cost from list_presets, then leases one render-lite machine with create_machine and waits with get_machine until it is ready. Places the asset on the machine with its add command (run_command), uploads a Blender Python script with upload_files, renders one 1920x1080 PNG with run_command (as a job followed with get_job if it runs long), and shows the PNG in the chat via download_files. Then calls release_machine and reports how long the machine ran and what it cost, plus the asset's credit line.

positive.description: A short Vork preview video, previewed and delivered as a link, then released.
positive.prompt: Make a 2-second 720p preview video with Vork of a simple scene: a chrome sphere on a grey floor. You have my OK to lease one render-lite machine; release it when done.
positive.tools_triggered: load_guide, estimate_render, create_machine, get_machine, run_command, upload_files, get_job, job_logs, download_files, release_machine
positive.expected_behavior: Loads the vork guide, estimates the 48-frame 720p preview with estimate_render and states the rough time and cost, then leases one render-lite machine and waits until it is ready. Runs vork setup, writes the scene, uploads it, and renders with the std/previs profile as a job, following it with get_job and job_logs. Downloads the output: the MP4 comes back as a download link given to the reviewer, with a still frame shown in the chat. Then releases the machine and reports its run time and cost.

positive.description: A 3D model is generated after an estimate and approval, then placed on a machine and rendered in Blender, then the machine is released.
positive.prompt: Generate a 3D model of a ceramic teapot with Voyager's default 3D model and render a 1080p studio still of it with Blender. You have my OK to spend the estimated credits and to lease one render-lite machine; release it when done.
positive.tools_triggered: estimate_3d_from_text, generate_3d_from_text, get_3d_job, create_machine, get_machine, place_3d_model, upload_files, run_command, download_files, release_machine
positive.expected_behavior: Calls estimate_3d_from_text with the prompt and the default 3D model and states the estimated credits, then calls generate_3d_from_text once with the same prompt and a client_key and polls the same job with get_3d_job until it succeeds (never submitting a second job), showing the preview and the GLB download link. Leases one render-lite machine with create_machine, waits with get_machine until it is ready, copies the GLB onto it with place_3d_model, uploads a Blender script with upload_files that imports the GLB, lights and frames it, and renders one 1920x1080 PNG with run_command. Downloads the PNG with download_files and shows it, then calls release_machine and reports how long the machine ran and its cost.

negative.description: A request for AI image generation is outside this plugin.
negative.prompt: Generate an AI image of a cat wearing a space helmet.
negative.expected_behavior: Calls no Voyager 3D tool and leases no machine: this plugin renders 3D scenes on cloud GPUs and does not generate AI images.

negative.description: A voiceover request is outside this plugin, which has no audio tools.
negative.prompt: Make a voiceover that says "Welcome to our studio" in a calm voice.
negative.expected_behavior: Calls no Voyager 3D tool, leases no machine and spends no credits: this plugin generates 3D models and renders 3D scenes and does not make speech or audio.

negative.description: A large render is estimated, not started, until the user approves the cost.
negative.prompt: Render a 60-second 4K Vork animation of a city flythrough.
negative.expected_behavior: Calls estimate_render for the job and reports the rough time and cost, including any multi-GPU recommendation, then asks the reviewer to approve before leasing. Calls no create_machine and spends no credits in this turn.

publication.release_notes: Corrected tool annotations: download_files is no longer marked read-only, since it creates download links. The idle-timeout guidance in the skill is now accurate.
